messages:
omar: FYI — GCP sent a revised EDP draft. Main changes: a 10% surge credit cap, a ‘backstop’ clause tying guaranteed capacity to an annual usage floor, and per-region carveouts that default to us if we don’t specify.
sophia: can you paste the exact language for the backstop clause? sounds risky for bursty jobs.
omar: sure, excerpt: "Provider may reduce committed capacity if Customer does not meet the Annual Consumption Floor; Provider will provide backstop credits equivalent to up to 10% of monthly committed capacity for transient surges."
liam: that wording basically lets them claw back unused reservation and call it a credit instead of capacity. credit != capacity. we need a hard cap on preemption or guaranteed baseline throughput for critical customers.
janet: agree. ops side — our fleet pattern is spiky for training and steady for inference. If they convert unused to a credit we still lose throughput when we need it.
gcp-account: thanks for the heads up. The intent behind backstop is to avoid idle reserved inventory. We can propose a modification: unused reserved capacity converts to credits only after a 90-day trailing utilization check and is subject to a 48-hour notice window during seasonal capacity adjustments.
sophia: sounds better. 48 hours is still scary during a big release though. can we add an emergency carveout for scheduled launches or critical oncall incidents? e.g., allow a single 7-day exception per quarter without triggering backstop.
gcp-account: that's reasonable to ask for. Also recommend adding explicit language that credits are redeemable toward compute at parity and can be applied across regions for 12 months.
liam: another red flag: per-region carveouts defaulting to us. If we forget to specify regions they auto-assign capacity where they like. we should require any region-level changes to be mutual or at least require 30 days notice.
omar: noted. also found a billing discrepancy in last month’s invoice that we should raise: SKU GPU_A100_40GB_US_WEST_1 — billed hours: 1,244; our cluster telemetry shows 980 billed by our meter. attached snippet from invoice: 
``
Invoice 2026-02-28
Line item: GPU_A100_40GB_US_WEST_1
Quantity billed: 1244 hours
Unit rate: $3.20/hr
Total: $3,980.80
```
janet: who on finance is owning that? we need meter logs to compare against provider's metering. billing-bot: automated billing report uploaded: https://storage.redwood/edp/invoices/2026-02-28.pdf :document: (sha256: ab12...)
sophia: pinging @billing-team to reconcile. liam, can you attach the cluster-side meter export (hourly aggregated) to this thread?
liam: attaching small sample below: 
``
2026-02-01T00:00Z GPU_A100_40GB_US_WEST_1 hours: 40
2026-02-01T01:00Z hours: 38
...
2026-02-28T23:00Z hours: 35
Total: 980
```
omar: two possibilities — provider meter includes preemptible/spot instances or counts accelerator attach time even when idle. we must ask for metering granularity and SKU mapping. also confirm whether their metering window is UTC vs local TZ.
gcp-account: we log both: preemptible usage is reported under a separate SKU, but we can request a line-by-line breakdown. if there's a mapping mismatch we'll correct it.
janet: action item for finance: open an invoice dispute referencing Invoice 2026-02-28 and request meta CSV with hourly metering, SKU mapping, and any internal rounding rules. target SLA for vendor reply: 5 business days.
sophia: on the EDP negotiation side, propose these concessions: 1) 90-day trailing utilization test before backstop activation; 2) single 7-day quarterly launch exception; 3) 30-day mutual notice for region moves; 4) surge credits redeemable across regions for 12 months at parity; 5) metering transparency appendix (hourly CSV + mapping).
liam: I'll draft suggested redlines. focus on preserving guaranteed baseline and limiting credit-only remediation. also propose a hard floor: during active incidents (pager escalation > P1 for infra), provider cannot reclaim reserved capacity for 7 days.
omar: good call. ops needs an automatic fallback: if capacity reclaimed, traffic should route to Dedicated fallback pool or queued with SLA degradation notice to product. add that to the runbook.
janet: finance notes — potential影響 (impact) to cost modeling: if they convert unused to credits we lose predictability. we should model worst-case effective capacity at -10% for first-year forecasts.
sophia: thumbs up. also ask them for an early termination credit schedule. we might want an escape if region latency/availability is worse than promised.
gcp-account: I'll see what legal and pricing teams will accept. happy to push the 90-day clause and the 7-day exception. region notice might be more sensitive but 30 days is within negotiation range.
billing-bot: billing-ticket #BT-468 created for Invoice 2026-02-28 discrepancy. Assigned to finance (janet). Estimated response: 3-5 business days.
liam: next steps: 1) Omar to produce a short redline doc with the above redlines (due EOD tomorrow). 2) Janet to submit invoice dispute and attach our meter export. 3) Sophia to prepare negotiation playbook and fallback runbook snippet. 4) GCP account to escalate to pricing/legal.
omar: drafting now. will post redline link when ready.
sophia: thanks — labelling this thread as high-priority. if we get capacity reclaimed mid-quarter we should trigger an immediate warroom. :rotating_light:
janet: noted. finance will keep a weekly monitoring digest of SKU deltas until EDP signed.
gcp-account: will follow up with internal teams and update here when I have the draft concession language.
liam: cool. if we get stuck we can propose a phased ramp: guaranteed baseline for 6 months then revisit utilization banding. often easier to sell than permanent floors.
omar: good negotiating lever. closing log: ticketed items and owners above, expected vendor reply by 5 business days.
